name: CSF Analysis
ssx: Severe headache, nausea, vomiting, photophobia, neck stiffness, fever, confusion, seizures
preparation: No special preparation. Performed via lumbar puncture by physician.
procedure: Collect cerebrospinal fluid through lumbar puncture. Send immediately to the laboratory for analysis (cell counts, glucose, protein, cultures).
purpose: To evaluate for central nervous system infections (meningitis, encephalitis), subarachnoid hemorrhage, inflammatory or autoimmune conditions (e.g., multiple sclerosis), malignancies, and other neurological disorders.

name: Body Fluid Analysis
ssx: Site-specific symptoms such as chest pain and dyspnea (pleural effusion), abdominal distension and pain (ascites), joint swelling and pain (synovial effusion), or chest discomfort and palpitations (pericardial effusion)
lo_ssx: Transudate: usually clear, low protein and LDH, due to systemic conditions (e.g., heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome)
hi_ssx: Exudate: cloudy or bloody, high protein and LDH, due to local pathology (e.g., infection, malignancy, inflammation, trauma)
preparation: No special preparation. Fluid is collected by physician via thoracentesis, paracentesis, pericardiocentesis, or arthrocentesis depending on site.
procedure: Collect appropriate body fluid under sterile conditions. Send to laboratory for cell count, differential, chemical analysis, microbiology, and cytology as needed.
specimen: Pleural, Peritoneal, Pericardial, or Synovial Fluid
purpose: To differentiate between transudate and exudate, evaluate for infection, malignancy, hemorrhage, or inflammatory conditions in body cavities or joints.

name: SEMINAL FLUID ANALYSIS
ssx: Male infertility, abnormal sperm count, erectile dysfunction, difficulty conceiving
lo_ssx: Low sperm count, poor motility, abnormal morphology, or low semen volume may indicate infertility or reproductive disorder
hi_ssx: Normal sperm concentration (>15 million/mL), motility (>40%), morphology (≥4% normal forms), and adequate volume (≥1.5 mL) suggest normal fertility potential
preparation: Abstinence from sexual activity for 3–5 days before collection.
procedure: Collect semen sample via masturbation into sterile container. Evaluate sperm count, motility, morphology, and other parameters.
purpose: To evaluate male fertility potential and investigate causes of infertility by assessing semen quality, sperm count, motility, morphology, and other seminal parameters.

name: CULTURE AND SENSITIVITY - BLOOD
ssx: Fever, chills, sepsis, unexplained infections, prolonged fever of unknown origin
lo_ssx: No microbial growth detected after incubation period (negative culture)
hi_ssx: Positive culture indicating presence of pathogenic microorganisms with antibiotic susceptibility pattern
preparation: No fasting required. Specimen collected aseptically prior to antibiotic therapy.
procedure: Collect blood aseptically and inoculate into blood culture bottles. Incubate and monitor for microbial growth. Perform sensitivity testing.
purpose: To detect bloodstream infections, identify causative organisms, and determine appropriate antibiotic therapy.

name: ACID FAST BACILLI STAIN
ssx: Cough lasting ≥3 weeks, hemoptysis, chest pain, weight loss, fever, night sweats, fatigue, loss of appetite
lo_ssx: No acid-fast bacilli observed in smear (negative result)
hi_ssx: Presence of acid-fast bacilli in smear (positive result), suggestive of tuberculosis or other mycobacterial infection
preparation: No special preparation; provide early morning sputum specimen on 3 consecutive days if possible.
procedure: Prepare sputum smear, heat-fix, stain with carbolfuchsin, decolorize with acid alcohol, counterstain with methylene blue. Examine microscopically for acid-fast bacilli.
specimen: Sputum (preferred), may also use gastric aspirates or bronchoalveolar lavage
purpose: To detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis and other acid-fast bacilli in respiratory and other specimens.

name: CULTURE AND SENSITIVITY / URINE
ssx: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic pain, flank pain, fever, chills
lo_ssx: No growth after incubation (negative urine culture)
hi_ssx: Growth of pathogenic bacteria with antibiotic susceptibility profile (positive urine culture)
preparation: Midstream clean-catch urine sample preferred. If catheterized, use sterile technique.
purpose: To detect urinary tract infections and guide appropriate antibiotic therapy.

name: CULTURE AND SENSITIVITY / BODY FLUID
ssx: Site-specific symptoms depending on fluid: pleural effusion (chest pain, dyspnea), peritoneal effusion (abdominal pain, distension), synovial effusion (joint pain, swelling)
hi_ssx: Positive growth of microorganisms with antibiotic susceptibility profile
preparation: Specimen collected aseptically by physician depending on site.
specimen: Body Fluid (pleural, peritoneal, pericardial, synovial, etc.)
purpose: To identify infectious agents in body fluids and determine appropriate antimicrobial therapy.

name: CULTURE AND SENSITIVITY / OTHER
ssx: Depends on suspected site of infection
hi_ssx: Positive microbial growth with antibiotic susceptibility profile
preparation: Specimen collected aseptically depending on clinical requirement.
specimen: Other specimen types (e.g., pus, wound swab, catheter tip, etc.)
purpose: To detect pathogens from non-routine specimens and guide antibiotic therapy.

name: RANDOM BLOOD SUGAR
ssx: Symptoms of abnormal glucose levels: hypoglycemia (sweating, shakiness, dizziness, confusion, seizures), hyperglycemia (frequent urination, excessive thirst, fatigue, blurred vision).
hi_ssx: Hyperglycemia: ≥200 mg/dL (suggestive of diabetes if symptomatic)
preparation: No fasting required. Sample may be collected at any time of day.
purpose: To assess blood glucose level at any time of day, useful for diabetes screening and monitoring.

name: FASTING BLOOD SUGAR
ssx: Symptoms of abnormal glucose levels: hypoglycemia (hunger, sweating, tremors, confusion, seizures), hyperglycemia (excessive thirst, frequent urination, nausea, fruity breath odor).
hi_ssx: Hyperglycemia: ≥126 mg/dL (diagnostic for diabetes if confirmed)
preparation: 8–10 hours fasting, no food or drinks except water before collection.
purpose: To measure fasting blood glucose level for the diagnosis and monitoring of diabetes mellitus.

name: GLYCOSYLATED HEMOGLOBIN
ssx: Long-term monitoring of blood glucose control in diabetic and pre-diabetic patients
lo_ssx: Possible hypoglycemia or over-treatment: sweating, shakiness, confusion
hi_ssx: Uncontrolled diabetes: frequent urination, excessive thirst, fatigue, poor wound healing
purpose: To assess average blood glucose levels over the past 2–3 months and monitor diabetes control

name: ALANINE AMINOTRANSFERASE
ssx: Often requested for suspected liver disease
lo_ssx: Low values usually not clinically significant; may be seen in nutrient deficiency or muscle wasting
hi_ssx: Liver injury: jaundice, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, fatigue, nausea
purpose: To detect and monitor liver injury or disease

name: ASPARTATE AMINOTRANSFERASE
ssx: Used to evaluate liver and muscle health
lo_ssx: Low values usually not clinically significant; may be seen in nutrient deficiency or muscle wasting
hi_ssx: Elevated in liver disease, myocardial infarction, or muscle injury: jaundice, muscle pain, abdominal pain, fatigue
purpose: To detect liver or muscle damage and monitor treatment response

name: TOTAL CHOLESTEROL
lo_ssx: Rare; usually no symptoms when too low
hi_ssx: Xanthomas, chest pain, risk of atherosclerosis
purpose: Measures overall cholesterol to assess risk of heart disease

name: TRIGLYCERIDES
hi_ssx: Pancreatitis, abdominal pain, fatty liver
purpose: Assesses fat storage and risk of metabolic syndrome & pancreatitis

name: High Density Lipoprotein-Cholesterol
hi_ssx: Usually no adverse symptoms; considered protective
purpose: Known as 'good cholesterol', helps remove excess cholesterol from blood

name: Low Density Lipoprotein-Cholesterol
hi_ssx: Atherosclerosis, chest pain, heart attack, stroke
purpose: Known as 'bad cholesterol', indicates risk of plaque buildup in arteries

name: VERY LOW DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN
lo_ssx: Usually not clinically significant when low
hi_ssx: Linked to insulin resistance, obesity, and fatty liver disease
purpose: Transports triglycerides; high levels increase risk of heart disease

name: Cholesterol/HDL Ratio
lo_ssx: Low ratio = protective; indicates lower cardiovascular risk
hi_ssx: High ratio = increased risk of heart attack and stroke
purpose: Assesses the balance between good (HDL) and total cholesterol for cardiovascular risk. A high cholesterol level is not always dangerous if HDL is also high.

name: LDL/HDL Ratio
lo_ssx: Low ratio = may indicate lower cardiovascular risk
hi_ssx: High ratio = associated with greater risk of atherosclerosis and heart disease due to plaque formation in arteries
purpose: Evaluates cardiovascular risk by comparing LDL (bad cholesterol) and HDL (good cholesterol) levels.

name: Creatinine
purpose: Assesses kidney function and filtration ability by measuring waste product from muscle metabolism.
lo_ssx: Low levels may indicate reduced muscle mass or certain liver disease
hi_ssx: Elevated in kidney dysfunction, dehydration, or muscle breakdown

name: BLOOD UREA NITROGEN
purpose: Assesses kidney function and protein metabolism by measuring nitrogen waste products in the blood.
lo_ssx: Fatigue, decreased urine output, confusion, hypotension
hi_ssx: Nausea, vomiting, edema, confusion, signs of uremia, pruritus
frequency: As needed or every 6-12 months (renal monitoring)

name: BLOOD URIC ACID
purpose: Evaluates uric acid metabolism for the diagnosis and monitoring of gout, kidney stones, and renal function.
lo_ssx: Fatigue, weakness, weight loss (rare, usually asymptomatic)
hi_ssx: Joint pain, swelling, redness (gout), kidney stones, fever

name: POTASSIUM
purpose: Measures potassium levels to evaluate electrolyte balance, kidney function, and cardiac status.
hi_ssx: Palpitations, arrhythmias, muscle weakness, cardiac arrest
preparation: Never give K to any patient who is not voiding. Limit K to 40 mEqs/L of fluid added to IVF.

name: CHLORIDE
purpose: Helps assess electrolyte and acid-base balance, especially in relation to sodium and bicarbonate levels.
lo_ssx: Muscle spasms, dehydration, confusion, respiratory alkalosis
hi_ssx: Fatigue, weakness, excessive thirst, hypertension, metabolic acidosis
frequency: Every 6-12 months or as needed (electrolyte monitoring)

name: SODIUM
purpose: Measures sodium levels to monitor fluid balance, kidney function, and neurological status.
lo_ssx: Headache, confusion, seizures, nausea, vomiting, coma (hyponatremia)
hi_ssx: Thirst, restlessness, irritability, seizures, coma (hypernatremia)
frequency: Every 6-12 months or as needed (electrolyte monitoring)

name: PHOSPHORUS, INORGANIC
lo_ssx: Muscle weakness, bone pain, confusion, respiratory failure
hi_ssx: Muscle cramps, tetany, hypotension, soft tissue calcification
purpose: Used to evaluate phosphate metabolism, kidney function, and bone disorders such as rickets and osteomalacia.

name: CALCIUM
lo_ssx: Muscle spasms, tingling, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias
hi_ssx: Constipation, kidney stones, abdominal pain, confusion
purpose: Assesses calcium balance, helpful in diagnosing bone disease, kidney disease, and parathyroid disorders.

name: CALCIUM, IONIZED
hi_ssx: Weakness, nausea, vomiting, cardiac arrhythmias
purpose: Measures the biologically active form of calcium; important in critically ill patients, surgery, and monitoring parathyroid function.

name: MAGNESIUM
lo_ssx: Tremors, seizures, muscle cramps, cardiac arrhythmias
hi_ssx: Nausea, hypotension, respiratory depression, loss of reflexes
purpose: Evaluates magnesium levels in relation to muscle, nerve, and cardiac function; also used in monitoring kidney disorders and malnutrition.

name: MAGNESIUM, URINE
lo_ssx: May reflect low dietary intake or renal wasting
hi_ssx: May indicate excessive supplementation or renal loss
purpose: Assesses urinary magnesium excretion to help differentiate causes of low or high blood magnesium levels.

name: ALKALINE PHOSPHATASE
lo_ssx: Delayed growth in children, bone pain, fatigue
hi_ssx: Bone disease (Paget’s, rickets), liver disease, jaundice, pruritus
purpose: To evaluate liver and bone health, useful in diagnosing liver disease, bone disorders, and bile duct obstructions.

name: TOTAL BILIRUBIN
hi_ssx: Jaundice, yellowing of eyes/skin, dark urine, fatigue
purpose: To assess liver function and diagnose jaundice, hemolysis, and bile duct obstruction.

name: Direct Bilirubin
hi_ssx: Obstructive jaundice, itching, pale stool, hepatobiliary disease
purpose: To assess liver function and diagnose jaundice, hemolysis, and bile duct obstruction.

name: Indirect Bilirubin
hi_ssx: Hemolytic anemia, neonatal jaundice, fatigue, pallor
purpose: To assess liver function and diagnose jaundice, hemolysis, and bile duct obstruction.

name: TOTAL PROTEIN
hi_ssx: Dehydration, nausea, elevated blood pressure
purpose: To evaluate protein levels in the blood and diagnose anemia, malnutrition, and kidney disease.

name: ALBUMIN
lo_ssx: Edema, ascites, delayed wound healing, fatigue
hi_ssx: Dehydration, diarrhea, high-protein diet, steroid use
frequency: As needed / kapag may liver o kidney disease monitoring
purpose: To assess nutritional status, liver function, and kidney disease by measuring the main protein in blood plasma.

name: GLOBULIN
lo_ssx: Frequent infections, immune deficiency, liver disease
hi_ssx: Chronic inflammation, multiple myeloma, autoimmune disease
purpose: To evaluate immune system function and detect chronic infections, liver disease, or certain blood cancers.

name: ALBUMIN/ GLOBULIN RATIO
lo_ssx: Liver disease, kidney disease, chronic infections
hi_ssx: Leukemia, genetic disorders, low globulin production
frequency: As needed / kapag abnormal ang Albumin o Globulin
purpose: To help differentiate between liver disease, kidney disease, and immune disorders by comparing albumin and globulin levels.

name: ALDOSTERONE
lo_ssx: Low blood pressure, dehydration, dizziness, salt craving
hi_ssx: Hypertension, muscle weakness, frequent urination, metabolic alkalosis
frequency: As ordered / kapag suspected adrenal disorder
purpose: To diagnose and monitor adrenal gland disorders such as hyperaldosteronism, Addison’s disease, and secondary hypertension.

name: LACTATE DEHYDROGENASE
hi_ssx: Tissue damage, hemolysis, myocardial infarction, liver disease, cancers
frequency: As needed / cancer or tissue damage monitoring
purpose: To assess tissue damage and aid in diagnosing conditions such as heart attack, liver disease, hemolysis, and cancer.

name: Gamma-Glutamyl Transferase
lo_ssx: Low: Rare, usually not clinically significant.
hi_ssx: High: Liver disease, bile duct obstruction, chronic alcohol use.
preparation: Fasting preferred; avoid alcohol before test
purpose: To evaluate liver and bile duct function, and to help detect alcohol-related liver damage.

name: Prolactin
hi_ssx: High: Galactorrhea, infertility, pituitary adenoma.
purpose: To evaluate pituitary gland function and investigate infertility, galactorrhea, or suspected pituitary tumors.

name: Serum Iron
lo_ssx: Low: Iron deficiency anemia, chronic disease.
hi_ssx: High: Hemochromatosis, hemolytic anemia, iron overload.
purpose: To measure circulating iron levels and help diagnose anemia, iron overload, or other iron metabolism disorders.

name: Total Iron Binding Capacity
lo_ssx: Low: Chronic disease, malnutrition, liver disease.
hi_ssx: High: Iron deficiency anemia, pregnancy.
purpose: To assess the blood’s capacity to transport iron and help distinguish between iron deficiency and other types of anemia.

name: Urobilinogen
lo_ssx: Low: Not clinically significant (may indicate antibiotic use).
hi_ssx: High: Liver disease, hemolytic anemia.
purpose: To evaluate liver function and detect hemolysis through measurement of urinary bilirubin breakdown products.

name: Acid Phosphatase
lo_ssx: Bone disease, prostate cancer (low activity is rare)
hi_ssx: Prostate carcinoma, bone metastasis, Paget's disease, Gaucher disease
preparation: Fasting preferred, avoid prostate manipulation prior to test
purpose: To assess prostate function and detect prostate cancer or bone-related disorders.

name: Myoglobin
lo_ssx: Not clinically significant (low values not used diagnostically)
hi_ssx: Acute myocardial infarction, skeletal muscle injury, renal failure
frequency: as ordered (stat in chest pain workup)
purpose: To detect early muscle injury, including myocardial infarction and rhabdomyolysis.

name: B-type Natriuretic Peptide
hi_ssx: Heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction, acute coronary syndrome
purpose: To diagnose and monitor heart failure and ventricular dysfunction.

name: Creatine Phosphokinase
hi_ssx: Myocardial infarction, rhabdomyolysis, muscular dystrophy, hypothyroidism
frequency: as ordered (serial every 6–8 hrs in MI workup)
preparation: Avoid intramuscular injections or vigorous exercise before test
purpose: To evaluate muscle damage and support the diagnosis of myocardial infarction or rhabdomyolysis.

name: Lipase
hi_ssx: Acute pancreatitis, pancreatic carcinoma, biliary obstruction, renal failure
frequency: as ordered (stat in acute abdominal pain)
purpose: To diagnose and monitor acute pancreatitis and other pancreatic disorders.

name: Amylase
hi_ssx: Acute pancreatitis, parotitis, perforated ulcer, intestinal obstruction
purpose: To diagnose and monitor acute pancreatitis and other pancreatic or salivary gland disorders.

name: Prothrombin Time
hi_ssx: Liver disease, vitamin K deficiency, warfarin therapy, DIC
purpose: To evaluate coagulation function and monitor warfarin therapy.

name: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time
hi_ssx: Hemophilia, heparin therapy, liver disease, DIC
purpose: To evaluate coagulation function and monitor heparin therapy.

name: Antibody Screening
hi_ssx: Presence of unexpected antibodies (risk for hemolytic transfusion reaction)
purpose: To detect unexpected antibodies that may cause transfusion reactions or hemolytic disease of the newborn.

name: Match Blood
hi_ssx: Incompatible match (risk of transfusion reaction)
purpose: To ensure donor-recipient blood compatibility before transfusion and prevent transfusion reactions.

name: Crossmatching
hi_ssx: Incompatible donor-recipient reaction
purpose: To confirm donor-recipient blood compatibility before transfusion and prevent transfusion reactions.

name: Complete Blood Count
hi_ssx: Polycythemia, leukocytosis, thrombocytosis
frequency: as ordered, routine check-up, pre-op, monitoring therapy
purpose: To evaluate overall blood health and detect conditions such as anemia, infection, and hematologic disorders.

name: Actual Platelet Count
lo_ssx: Thrombocytopenia: bleeding risk, petechiae, spontaneous hemorrhage
hi_ssx: Thrombocytosis: clotting risk, myeloproliferative disorders
purpose: To measure platelet levels and diagnose bleeding or clotting disorders.

name: Bleeding Time
hi_ssx: Platelet function disorders, thrombocytopenia, von Willebrand disease
frequency: as ordered (rarely used, replaced by platelet function assays)
purpose: To assess platelet function and screen for bleeding disorders.

name: Clotting Time
hi_ssx: Hemophilia, clotting factor deficiencies, anticoagulant therapy
frequency: as ordered (rarely used; replaced by PT/aPTT)
purpose: To assess overall clotting ability and help diagnose bleeding disorders.

name: Reticulocyte Count
lo_ssx: Aplastic anemia, bone marrow suppression, iron deficiency anemia
hi_ssx: Hemolytic anemia, acute blood loss, response to therapy (iron, B12, folate)
purpose: To evaluate bone marrow activity and monitor treatment response in anemia.

name: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate
lo_ssx: Polycythemia vera, sickle cell anemia, leukocytosis (not usually clinically significant)
hi_ssx: Infections, autoimmune diseases, chronic inflammation, malignancy
purpose: To detect and monitor inflammation and inflammatory conditions.

name: Hemoglobin/Hematocrit
hi_ssx: Polycythemia: headache, dizziness, hypertension, thrombotic risk
frequency: as ordered, routine check-up, anemia/polycythemia monitoring
purpose: To evaluate red blood cell levels and diagnose anemia or polycythemia.

name: Hematocrit/Platelet
hi_ssx: Polycythemia (high HCT), thrombocytosis (clotting risk)
purpose: To assess red blood cell and platelet levels and diagnose anemia, polycythemia, or bleeding/clotting disorders.

name: Blood Typing + Rh
hi_ssx: N/A (result is categorical: A, B, AB, O; Rh+ or Rh−)
purpose: To determine ABO blood group and Rh factor for transfusion compatibility and pregnancy management.

name: Pregnancy Test
lo_ssx: Negative (may be false-negative in very early gestation)
hi_ssx: Positive (pregnancy, trophoblastic disease, or some tumors)
frequency: As ordered (confirmation of pregnancy, pre-procedural testing)
purpose: To detect pregnancy through the presence of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG).

name: Human Immunodeficiency Virus 1/2 Screening
hi_ssx: Positive (requires confirmatory testing: Western blot, ELISA, or NAAT)
frequency: As ordered (screening, diagnostic, prenatal, or high-risk assessment)
purpose: To screen for HIV infection.

name: Rapid Plasma Reagin (RPR) / VDRL Screening
hi_ssx: Positive (suggestive of syphilis; confirmatory testing with FTA-ABS or TPHA required)
frequency: As ordered (STI screening, prenatal, blood donation)
purpose: To screen for syphilis infection.

name: Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Screening
lo_ssx: Jaundice in newborn, pallor, dark urine, fatigue, shortness of breath
hi_ssx: Usually asymptomatic (high enzyme activity has no clinical significance)
purpose: To screen for G6PD deficiency, which may cause hemolytic anemia under oxidative stress.

name: Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Confirmatory
lo_ssx: Hemolytic anemia, jaundice, dark urine after fava beans, certain drugs, or infections
hi_ssx: No clinical consequence (high activity is rare and not associated with disease)
purpose: To confirm G6PD deficiency in patients with low enzyme activity on screening tests.

name: Dengue DUO (Ag/Ab) Screening
lo_ssx: Possible early infection (<24h) or absence of dengue
hi_ssx: Fever >24h, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, rash, bleeding tendencies
preparation: At least 24 hours of fever before testing
preference: For screening only. Interpretation: NS1 positive = acute infection (1–7 days); IgM positive = recent/ongoing infection; IgG positive = past infection or secondary dengue.
purpose: To screen for dengue using both antigen (NS1) and antibody (IgG/IgM) detection.

name: Dengue Antibody (IgG/IgM) Screening
lo_ssx: Asymptomatic or mild fever, body weakness
hi_ssx: Fever >24h, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, rash, bleeding tendencies
frequency: As ordered (suspected or past dengue infection)
preparation: At least 24 hours of fever before testing
preference: For screening only. Interpretation: IgM positive = recent/ongoing infection; IgG positive = past infection or secondary dengue.
purpose: To screen for dengue infection using antibody detection (IgG/IgM).

name: Dengue Antigen (NS1) Screening
hi_ssx: Fever >24h, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, rash, bleeding tendencies
preparation: At least 24 hours of fever before testing
preference: For screening only. Interpretation: NS1 positive = acute dengue infection (1–7 days).
purpose: To screen for dengue infection using antigen detection (NS1).

name: Potassium Hydroxide Smear (10%)
lo_ssx: No fungal elements seen (does not rule out infection if symptoms persist)
hi_ssx: Itching, scaling, redness, whitish patches, brittle/thickened nails, hair loss in affected area
purpose: To detect fungal infections using a 10% potassium hydroxide (KOH) smear.

name: Malarial Smear
lo_ssx: No malarial parasites seen (repeat testing may be required if fever persists)
hi_ssx: Chills, intermittent fever, sweating, headache, anemia, splenomegaly
frequency: As ordered (febrile illness, travel history to endemic area)
purpose: To diagnose malaria by detecting malarial parasites in blood smears.

name: Hepatitis A Virus Screening
hi_ssx: Acute hepatitis: fatigue, fever, abdominal pain, jaundice, dark urine, pale stools
frequency: As ordered (suspected acute hepatitis, screening in high-risk groups)
purpose: To screen for acute or past hepatitis A virus infection.

name: Anti-Hepatitis A Virus IgG
lo_ssx: No evidence of past infection or immunity
hi_ssx: Indicates past infection or immunity (post-vaccination or recovery)
purpose: To determine past infection or immunity to hepatitis A virus.

name: Anti-Hepatitis A Virus IgM
hi_ssx: Acute or recent HAV infection with jaundice, abdominal pain, anorexia
frequency: As ordered (suspected acute hepatitis A infection)
purpose: To detect acute or recent hepatitis A virus infection.

name: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Screening
lo_ssx: Negative: no evidence of active infection
hi_ssx: Positive: may indicate acute or chronic hepatitis B infection (jaundice, fatigue, hepatomegaly)
frequency: As ordered (screening, suspected hepatitis, prenatal testing)
purpose: To screen for hepatitis B virus infection.

name: Hepatitis B Envelope Antigen
lo_ssx: Negative: low infectivity or inactive infection
hi_ssx: Positive: high infectivity, active viral replication
frequency: As ordered (monitoring hepatitis B infection and infectivity)
purpose: To assess hepatitis B infectivity and viral replication activity.

name: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Titer
lo_ssx: Low/undetectable titer: no active infection or resolved past infection
hi_ssx: High titer: active infection, either acute or chronic, with possible symptoms of hepatitis
frequency: As ordered (monitoring hepatitis B infection and treatment response)
purpose: To quantify hepatitis B surface antigen levels for monitoring infection status and treatment response.

name: Hepatitis C Virus Screening
hi_ssx: Positive: possible chronic HCV infection; symptoms may include fatigue, hepatomegaly, elevated liver enzymes
frequency: As ordered (screening or suspected hepatitis C)
purpose: To screen for hepatitis C virus infection.

name: Fecalysis
lo_ssx: Normal: no parasites, no WBC/RBC, normal stool consistency
hi_ssx: Abnormal: presence of parasites (Giardia, Entamoeba), ova, cysts, blood, or fat malabsorption
frequency: As ordered (diarrhea, abdominal pain, suspected parasitic infection)
purpose: To detect parasites, ova, cysts, and other abnormalities in stool.

name: Occult Blood
lo_ssx: No hidden blood detected in stool
hi_ssx: Hidden GI bleeding, may suggest peptic ulcer, gastritis, colon polyp, or colorectal cancer
frequency: As ordered (screening for GI bleeding, anemia, colorectal cancer)
preparation: Avoid red meat, certain vegetables, and iron supplements 48–72 hours before test
purpose: To detect hidden (occult) blood in stool, useful for diagnosing gastrointestinal bleeding.

name: Apt-Downey Test
lo_ssx: Blood in stool is of maternal origin (not from infant)
hi_ssx: Blood in stool/infant vomitus is fetal in origin (possible neonatal GI bleeding)
frequency: As ordered (evaluation of neonatal GI bleeding)
purpose: To determine whether the blood in stool or infant vomitus is of maternal or fetal origin.

name: Papanicolaou Smear
lo_ssx: Negative: normal cervical cells, no dysplasia or malignancy
hi_ssx: Abnormal: cervical dysplasia, atypical squamous cells, or possible cervical cancer (may present with postcoital bleeding, abnormal vaginal discharge, pelvic pain)
frequency: Every 3 years for women aged 21–65 if results are normal
preparation: Avoid douching, intercourse, or vaginal medications 48 hours before test
purpose: To screen for cervical cancer and precancerous changes in cervical cells.
description: A procedure in which a small brush is used to gently remove cells from the surface of the cervix and the area around it so they can be checked under a microscope for cervical cancer or precancerous changes.

name: Peripheral Blood Smear
lo_ssx: Normal morphology of red cells, white cells, and platelets
hi_ssx: Abnormal cell morphology: anemia (microcytic, macrocytic, sickle cells), leukemia (blasts), infections (malarial parasites)
frequency: As ordered (suspected anemia, leukemia, or infections)
purpose: To evaluate blood cell morphology and diagnose hematologic disorders.

name: Anti-Hepatitis B Core IgM
hi_ssx: Positive: acute or recent HBV infection, may present with jaundice, anorexia, fatigue, hepatomegaly
purpose: To detect acute or recent hepatitis B infection.

name: Anti-Hepatitis B Core IgG
hi_ssx: Positive: indicates past or chronic HBV infection; may be asymptomatic or present with chronic hepatitis symptoms
frequency: As ordered (screening past or chronic HBV)
purpose: To detect past exposure or chronic hepatitis B infection.

name: Anti-Hepatitis B Envelope IgG
lo_ssx: Negative: absence of HBe antibody, may indicate ongoing replication
hi_ssx: Positive: usually indicates low infectivity or recovery phase from HBV infection
purpose: To assess hepatitis B infection status, infectivity, and recovery phase.

name: Anti-Hepatitis B Envelope IgM
lo_ssx: Negative: no evidence of acute HBe response
hi_ssx: Positive: suggests recent/acute HBV infection and seroconversion phase
purpose: To detect acute hepatitis B infection and seroconversion phase.

name: Anti-Hepatitis C Virus Titer
lo_ssx: Negative: no evidence of HCV infection
hi_ssx: Positive: indicates exposure to HCV; may represent chronic infection. Symptoms: fatigue, elevated liver enzymes, hepatomegaly, risk of cirrhosis
frequency: As ordered (screening or monitoring HCV infection)
purpose: To quantify antibodies against hepatitis C virus and help evaluate exposure or chronic infection.

name: Anti-Hepatitis C Virus
lo_ssx: Negative: no evidence of HCV infection
hi_ssx: Positive: indicates exposure to HCV; may represent chronic infection. Symptoms: fatigue, elevated liver enzymes, hepatomegaly, risk of cirrhosis
purpose: To screen for hepatitis C virus infection.

name: Oral Glucose Tolerance Test
lo_ssx: Normal: FBS <100 mg/dl, 2-hr post glucose <140 mg/dl (no symptoms)
hi_ssx: Diabetes: FBS ≥126 mg/dl or 2-hr ≥200 mg/dl; discontinue if FBS is more than 180 mg/dl. Symptoms: polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia, weight loss
frequency: As necessary (diagnosis of diabetes or during pregnancy for gestational diabetes)
preparation: 8–12 hours fasting; avoid strenuous activity before test
purpose: To diagnose diabetes mellitus and impaired glucose tolerance.

name: Creatine Phosphokinase MM
lo_ssx: Normal: no evidence of skeletal muscle damage
hi_ssx: Elevated in muscular dystrophy, trauma, rhabdomyolysis, intense exercise. Symptoms: muscle weakness, myalgia, dark urine
frequency: As ordered (suspected muscle injury or disease)
purpose: To evaluate skeletal muscle damage.

name: Creatine Phosphokinase MB
hi_ssx: Elevated in myocardial infarction, myocarditis, cardiac trauma. Symptoms: chest pain, dyspnea, diaphoresis, palpitations
purpose: To evaluate cardiac muscle injury, especially myocardial infarction.

name: Creatinine Clearance
lo_ssx: Low: indicates renal impairment; symptoms may include oliguria, edema, fatigue
hi_ssx: High: may be seen in pregnancy, high protein intake, or hyperfiltration states
purpose: To assess renal function and estimate glomerular filtration rate (GFR).

name: Testosterone
lo_ssx: Low: male—fatigue, decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, loss of muscle mass; female—irregular menses, infertility
hi_ssx: High: male—aggressiveness, acne, polycythemia; female—hirsutism, virilization, acne, polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS)
purpose: To evaluate androgen status and diagnose hormonal imbalances.

name: Pancreatic and Gastrointestinal Cancer Marker
lo_ssx: Normal: low levels, no clinical significance

name: Microalbumin Test (Urine)
lo_ssx: Low values are usually normal, no symptoms
hi_ssx: High values may indicate early kidney damage, often asymptomatic initially
frequency: Usually yearly for diabetics or hypertensive patients; per physician request
preference: Random urine or first morning urine; preferred first morning
preparation: No special preparation required; avoid strenuous exercise 24 hrs before test
purpose: Detects early kidney damage by measuring small amounts of albumin in urine; important for monitoring diabetics and hypertensive patients

name: X-ray Scoliosis Series
lo_ssx: Normal spinal alignment without evidence of curvature.
hi_ssx: Abnormal lateral curvature of the spine; Cobb angle > 10° indicates scoliosis.
preparation: Remove metallic objects; wear hospital gown; patient should stand upright for full spine imaging.
purpose: To evaluate and measure spinal curvature, monitor progression of scoliosis, and assess treatment outcomes.

name: X-ray Coccyx AP/L
lo_ssx: Normal coccyx alignment without fracture or dislocation.
hi_ssx: Evidence of fracture, dislocation, or abnormal angulation of the coccyx.
preparation: Remove metallic objects near pelvic area; patient positioned supine and lateral for imaging.
purpose: To evaluate coccygeal pain, trauma, or suspected fractures/dislocations.

name: X-ray Cervical Spine (C-spine) AP/L/O
lo_ssx: Normal cervical alignment, intact vertebrae, and preserved disc spaces.
hi_ssx: Evidence of fracture, dislocation, degenerative changes, or abnormal curvature.
preparation: Remove metallic objects around head and neck; patient positioned for AP, lateral, and oblique views.
purpose: To assess cervical spine alignment, detect fractures, degenerative changes, or evaluate trauma and chronic neck pain.

name: Axilla Bilateral Ultrasound
purpose: To evaluate axillary lymph nodes, masses, or abnormalities.

name: Biophysical Scoring 1 Fetus
preparation: Full bladder may be required; standard OB ultrasound prep.
purpose: To assess fetal well-being using biophysical scoring (single fetus).

name: Biophysical Scoring 2 Fetus
preparation: Full bladder may be required; standard OB ultrasound prep.
purpose: To assess fetal well-being using biophysical scoring (twins).

name: Chest Mapping Ultrasound
preparation: Expose chest area; remove metallic objects.
purpose: To evaluate chest tissues, masses, or abnormalities.

name: Chest Ultrasound
preparation: Expose chest area; remove metallic objects.
purpose: To detect pleural effusion, masses, or lung abnormalities.

name: Chest Ultrasound Bilateral
purpose: To evaluate bilateral chest tissues, masses, or fluid accumulation.

name: Hepatobiliary + Pancreas Ultrasound
preparation: Fasting required; remove metallic objects from abdomen.
purpose: To assess liver, gallbladder, and pancreas for masses or abnormalities.

name: Inguinal and Scrotal Ultrasound
preparation: Expose inguinal and scrotal area; remove metallic objects.
purpose: To detect hernias, masses, or abnormalities in inguinal and scrotal regions.

name: Joint Extremities Ultrasound
preparation: Expose joint area; remove jewelry or metallic objects.
purpose: To evaluate joint abnormalities, effusions, or soft tissue lesions.

name: KUB + Prostate Ultrasound
preparation: Full bladder required; remove metallic objects from abdomen.
purpose: To assess kidneys, bladder, and prostate for abnormalities.

name: OB Pregnant Ultrasound (1 fetus)
preparation: Full bladder recommended; standard OB prep.
purpose: To evaluate fetal growth, anatomy, and well-being for a single fetus.

name: OB Pregnant Ultrasound (2 fetus)
preparation: Full bladder recommended; standard OB prep.
purpose: To evaluate fetal growth, anatomy, and well-being for twins.

name: Scrotal with Doppler Ultrasound
preparation: Expose scrotal area; remove metallic objects.
purpose: To evaluate scrotal blood flow, masses, or abnormalities.

name: Single Organ Ultrasound
preparation: Expose target organ; remove metallic objects.
purpose: To evaluate a specific organ for pathology.

name: Transrectal Ultrasound
purpose: To assess prostate and rectal structures for abnormalities.

name: Urinary Bladder Ultrasound
purpose: To evaluate bladder volume, wall, and detect stones or masses.

name: Bladder + Prostate Ultrasound
preparation: Full bladder required; remove metallic objects from pelvis.
purpose: To evaluate both bladder and prostate for abnormalities.

name: 24Hrs ABPM
preparation: Attach ABPM cuff to patient’s arm; patient should keep normal activity but avoid vigorous exercise.
purpose: To monitor blood pressure variations over 24 hours.

name: 24hrs Holter Monitoring
preparation: Attach Holter monitor electrodes; patient should keep a diary of symptoms and activities.
purpose: To detect arrhythmias, ischemic changes, or conduction abnormalities over 24 hours.

name: Fibroscan
preparation: Fasting may be required; patient positioned supine with right arm raised.
purpose: To assess liver stiffness and fibrosis.

name: Bicarbonate / Total CO2
preparation: Standard blood chemistry prep; fasting may be required.
purpose: To evaluate acid-base status and bicarbonate levels.

name: Urine Albumin : Creatinine Ratio
purpose: To assess kidney function; calculate albumin-creatinine ratio.
note: Urine creatinine and protein included; only ratio calculated

name: Urine Protein : Creatinine Ratio
purpose: To detect proteinuria and assess kidney function; calculate protein-creatinine ratio.
note: Creatinine and protein included; only ratio calculated

name: Urine Microalbumin : Creatinine Ratio
purpose: To detect microalbuminuria; calculate microalbumin-creatinine ratio.

name: Vitamin B9 / Folate
preparation: Fasting may be required; standard blood chemistry prep.
purpose: To assess folate levels in blood.

name: X-ray Abdomen
preparation: Remove metallic objects from the abdomen area.
purpose: To evaluate abdominal organs and detect abnormal gas patterns, obstructions, or masses.

name: Apillordotic View
purpose: Specialized X-ray view to evaluate spinal curvature or thoracic vertebrae.

name: X-RAY Os Calcis (Axial/Lat)
preparation: Remove footwear and metallic objects around the foot.
purpose: To detect fractures or bone abnormalities of the calcaneus.

name: X-ray Patella (Skyview)
preparation: Remove metallic objects around the knee.
purpose: To assess patellar fractures, dislocations, or degenerative changes.

name: X-ray Toes
preparation: Remove footwear and jewelry on toes.
purpose: To evaluate fractures, dislocations, or degenerative changes in toes.

name: X-ray Mastoid (Townes/O/Open Mount)
preparation: Remove metallic objects around the head.
purpose: To evaluate mastoid air cells for infection or abnormality.

name: X-ray Chest Decubitus
preparation: Remove metallic objects on chest and upper body.
purpose: To detect pleural effusion or other chest abnormalities.

name: CT-Scan Plain of the Chest
preparation: Remove metallic objects on chest; follow CT scan protocol.
purpose: To evaluate thoracic organs, vessels, and detect masses, infections, or trauma.

name: CT-Scan Plain Cranial (Trauma)
preparation: Remove metallic objects from head; follow CT trauma protocol.
purpose: To detect cranial fractures, hemorrhage, or trauma-related abnormalities.

name: CT Scan Plain Cranial
purpose: To evaluate intracranial structures for lesions, hemorrhage, or abnormalities.

name: CT-Scan Upper Abdomen
preparation: Fasting may be required; remove metallic objects from abdomen.
purpose: To detect liver, pancreas, gallbladder, and spleen abnormalities.

name: CT Scan Stonogram
preparation: Hydration recommended; remove metallic objects from abdomen.
purpose: To detect urinary stones and urinary tract abnormalities.

name: CT Scan Whole Abdomen
preparation: Fasting may be required; remove metallic objects from abdomen.
purpose: To evaluate abdominal organs, detect masses, or trauma-related changes.

name: Urine Microalbumin
preparation: Collect a clean-catch midstream urine sample.
purpose: For early detection of kidney damage (microalbuminuria), especially in patients with diabetes or hypertension; may be used with urine creatinine to calculate the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR).

name: Lipoprotein A
preparation: Fasting for 9–12 hours prior to blood collection is recommended.
purpose: To assess cardiovascular risk by measuring Lipoprotein (a) levels; elevated Lp(a) is associated with increased risk of atherosclerosis, coronary artery disease, and stroke.
ssx: Often asymptomatic; high levels are a risk factor for premature cardiovascular disease, atherosclerosis, coronary artery disease, and stroke.
lo_ssx: Low or normal Lp(a) levels indicate no significant additional cardiovascular risk from this marker.
hi_ssx: Elevated Lp(a) levels are associated with increased risk of atherosclerosis, coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, and stroke.

name: Adrenocorticotropic Hormone
preparation: Patient should fast for 9–12 hours prior to specimen collection. Blood should be collected between 7:00–9:00 AM in a chilled EDTA tube, kept on ice, and transported immediately to the laboratory for processing.
purpose: To assess the function of the pituitary and adrenal glands by measuring ACTH concentration. This test helps diagnose adrenal insufficiency, Cushing’s syndrome, and other disorders affecting cortisol production and regulation.
ssx: Symptoms related to abnormal ACTH levels may include fatigue, muscle weakness, weight loss or gain, low or high blood pressure, changes in skin pigmentation, and features of cortisol excess such as central obesity and moon facies.
lo_ssx: Low ACTH levels suggest secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary or hypothalamic dysfunction, or suppression from exogenous corticosteroid therapy or adrenal tumors producing excess cortisol.
hi_ssx: High ACTH levels may indicate primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison’s disease), pituitary overproduction (Cushing’s disease), or ectopic ACTH secretion by non-pituitary tumors such as small-cell lung carcinoma.
